# clumsy

> clumsy degrades live network traffic on purpose - latency, jitter, packet
> loss, outages, reordering, corruption, bandwidth caps - so you can watch how
> an application behaves on a bad connection. It intercepts real packets
> system-wide (WinDivert on Windows, NFQUEUE on Linux): no proxy, and no change
> to the application under test. It is driven by command line options and a
> local REST API. This file is the usage guide for AI agents and scripts.

A Korean edition with the same content is served at `/llms_kr.txt`.

Three references are generated from the running code and are always current.
Prefer them over anything you remember about clumsy or about similar tools
(tc/netem, Network Link Conditioner, toxiproxy): the option names differ.

- `clumsy --help`      every option, every module parameter with its range
                       and default, and the exit codes. Needs no privileges.
- `GET /api/docs`      every REST endpoint with an example body.
- `GET /api/modules`   every module with a description, its parameters
                       (key, type, min, max, options) and their current values.


## Rules that prevent the usual mistakes

1. Nothing is shaped until a capture is running. A capture starts with
   `--filter` on the command line or `POST /api/filter`. Enabling modules
   without a filter does nothing, and reports no error.
2. Every option is a `--key value` pair. Switches are spelled out:
   `--lag on`, never a bare `--lag`.
3. A module has to be switched on AND configured: `--lag on --lag-time 100`.
   `--lag-time 100` alone sets a value on a module that stays off.
4. Chances are percentages from 0 to 100. `--drop-chance 5` is 5%.
   Times are milliseconds. Bandwidth is kilobytes per second.
5. Capturing needs privileges: an Administrator console on Windows,
   CAP_NET_ADMIN (or sudo) on Linux. Check `"admin"` in `GET /api/status`.
   If it is false, tell the user to start the terminal elevated; you cannot
   fix this from an unprivileged shell.
6. Always pass `--timeout <seconds>` when you launch clumsy. It is the safety
   net: a clumsy you forget to stop keeps degrading the user's network.
7. Keep the filter narrow - the port or address of the application under
   test. A broad filter (`true`, `tcp`, `outbound`) also shapes the user's
   browser, your own API connection, and clumsy's own control port.
8. clumsy runs until it is told to stop. Launch it in the background, then
   poll `GET /api/health` until it answers.
9. Only one clumsy can run at a time (exit code 4 otherwise). If one is
   already running, drive that one over REST or stop it with `POST /api/quit`.
10. Read the whole reply. A REST reply can be `"status":"ok"` and still carry
    `"unknownKeys"` (a key no module has) or `"warnings"` (a value that was
    clamped or not applied). `"params"` shows what is actually in effect, and
    `"capturing": false` means the setting is stored but nothing is being
    shaped yet. A request in which no key at all was usable is an error (400).
11. When you are done, stop it: `POST /api/quit`. Then tell the user the
    network is back to normal.


## Picking a module

Modules run in this order on every captured packet. All start switched off.
Every module also takes `<module>-inbound` and `<module>-outbound` (on|off,
both default on) to limit it to one direction.

| To reproduce                         | Module    | Parameters (range, default)                                   |
|--------------------------------------|-----------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| constant extra latency               | lag       | lag-time 0..15000 ms (50)                                     |
| unstable latency                     | jitter    | jitter-min, jitter-max 0..5000 ms (20, 100); jitter-dist uniform/normal/pareto (uniform) |
| evenly spread packet loss            | drop      | drop-chance 0..100 % (10)                                     |
| loss that comes in bursts            | burstloss | burstloss-good, burstloss-bad: drop % in the good/bad state (2, 80); burstloss-gb, burstloss-bg: % chance per packet to switch good->bad, bad->good (5, 20) |
| total outage, repeating              | blackout  | blackout-duration 100..60000 ms (3000); blackout-gap 1000..300000 ms of normal traffic between outages (15000); blackout-trigger: action, start/stop an outage now |
| stutter: hold, then release at once  | throttle  | throttle-frame 0..1000 ms (30); throttle-chance 0..100 % (10); throttle-drop on/off: drop instead of release (off) |
| duplicated packets                   | duplicate | duplicate-count 2..50 copies (2); duplicate-chance 0..100 % (10) |
| packets arriving out of order        | ood       | ood-chance 0..100 % (10); ood-buffer 2..50 packets (5); ood-delay 10..2000 ms (200) |
| corrupted application data           | tamper    | tamper-chance 0..100 % (10); tamper-position 0=front 1=center 2=back 3=random (1); tamper-checksum on/off: fix checksums so the damage reaches the app (on) |
| bit errors (noisy wireless link)     | corrupt   | corrupt-chance 0..100 % of packets (10); corrupt-ber 0..1000000 flipped bits per million (100); corrupt-checksum on/off (on) |
| TCP connections torn down            | reset     | reset-chance 0..100 % (0); reset-next: action, reset the next packet |
| slow link                            | bandwidth | bandwidth-bandwidth 0..99999 KB/s (10)                        |

On the command line each key is prefixed with `--`. In REST bodies and
scenario files the same keys are used without the dashes.

Typical mixes:

| Condition        | Settings                                                          |
|------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Mobile 4G        | lag 80 ms, drop 2 %, throttle 10 %                                |
| Mobile 3G        | lag 150 ms, drop 5 %, bandwidth 500 KB/s                          |
| Satellite        | lag 500 ms, drop 1 %                                              |
| Unstable Wi-Fi   | jitter 20..200 ms, burstloss good 2 / bad 80                      |
| Tunnel / lift    | blackout: a 3000 ms outage after every 30000 ms of traffic        |

Notes on values:

- Modules stack. Each enabled module acts on what the previous ones let
  through, so `drop` 5 % plus `burstloss` loses more than either alone.
- blackout alternates `blackout-gap` ms of normal traffic with
  `blackout-duration` ms of outage. "2 s down every 20 s" is duration 2000,
  gap 18000.
- burstloss defaults spend about 20 % of the time in the bad state, which
  averages near 18 % loss. For milder bursts lower `burstloss-gb` (how often a
  burst starts) or `burstloss-bad` (how lossy a burst is).
- bandwidth is in kilobytes per second (1 KB = 1024 bytes), not kilobits.
  A limit of 0 blocks everything: nothing is released from the queue.
- The actions `blackout-trigger` and `reset-next` are ignored unless their
  module is already on and a capture is running. Switch the module on and
  start the capture first, then send the action in a separate request.


## Writing a filter

The filter decides which packets clumsy touches; everything else passes
untouched. The syntax is the WinDivert filter language.

    udp and udp.DstPort == 7777                          one UDP port, outbound to it
    udp and (udp.DstPort == 7777 or udp.SrcPort == 7777) both directions of that port
    tcp and (tcp.DstPort == 443 or tcp.SrcPort == 443)   all HTTPS
    ip.DstAddr == 10.0.0.5 or ip.SrcAddr == 10.0.0.5     one remote host
    outbound and udp                                     everything UDP leaving this machine
    outbound and loopback                                localhost-to-localhost traffic

- Building blocks: `and` `or` `not` and parentheses; `inbound` `outbound`
  `loopback`; `tcp` `udp` `icmp` `ip` `ipv6`; `ip.SrcAddr` `ip.DstAddr`
  `tcp.SrcPort` `tcp.DstPort` `udp.SrcPort` `udp.DstPort`; `==` `!=` `<` `>`
  `<=` `>=`.
- Loopback traffic only ever matches as `outbound`; write
  `outbound and loopback`, never `inbound and loopback`.
- To exclude something, wrap a positive test in `not ( ... )`. A bare
  `tcp.DstPort != 8080` is false for every non-TCP packet, so it silently
  removes all UDP from the match.
- clumsy's own REST API is TCP on 127.0.0.1, port 8080 unless `--web-port`
  changed it. If the filter matches loopback TCP, exclude that port or heavy
  loss will lock you out of the API (put your own port in place of 8080):
  `outbound and loopback and not (tcp.DstPort == 8080 or tcp.SrcPort == 8080)`
- A test on one port (`udp.DstPort == 7777`) only matches packets going TO
  that port. To shape the replies as well, test both `DstPort` and `SrcPort`
  as in the second example above.
- `--process game.exe` (or `"process"` in `POST /api/filter`) additionally
  limits the capture to the ports that process has open right now.
- `GET /api/presets` returns ready-made named filters (game engines, etc.).
- A filter that does not parse fails the start with a message; fix it and
  try again.


## Recipe A: one timed run, command line only

Use this when the conditions stay the same for the whole test.

    clumsy --filter "udp and udp.DstPort == 7777" --lag on --lag-time 150 --drop on --drop-chance 5 --timeout 60 --stats-log stats.csv --report-out report.html

It exits by itself after 60 seconds with code 0, leaving `stats.csv` (one
row per second) and `report.html`. Run it in the background while you drive
the application under test, or in the foreground if the test runs elsewhere.
The output files are only written while a capture is running: after an exit
code of 3 there is no file, and that is not a separate problem.

This example shapes packets going to port 7777 only. Use the two-sided
filter from the section above to shape the replies too.

Exit codes:

    0  clean exit (--timeout reached, Ctrl+C, POST /api/quit)
    2  bad command line: unknown option, unusable value, or a --profile /
       --scenario that could not be loaded. Nothing was started. The message
       on stderr names the option and suggests the right spelling.
    3  the capture (--filter) or replay (--replay-in) could not start: not
       elevated, or the filter did not parse. Nothing is being shaped.
    4  another clumsy is already running.


## Recipe B: start once, change conditions over REST

Use this when conditions change during the test, or you need to read
statistics while it runs. The base URL is `http://127.0.0.1:8080` unless
`--web-port` says otherwise.

1. Launch in the background, with no filter yet and a generous timeout:

       clumsy --timeout 600 --stats-console 0

2. Wait until `GET /api/health` returns `{"status":"ok",...}`.
3. `GET /api/status` - stop here and report to the user if `"admin"` is false.
4. Configure the modules in one request:

       POST /api/apply
       {"lag":true,"lag-time":150,"drop":true,"drop-chance":5}

   The reply echoes what is now in effect:
   `{"status":"ok","applied":4,"capturing":false,"params":{"lag":"true","lag-time":"150","drop":"true","drop-chance":"5.0"}}`

5. Start capturing:

       POST /api/filter
       {"filter":"udp and udp.DstPort == 7777"}

6. Run the test. Change conditions at any time with `POST /api/apply` or
   `POST /api/modules/{name}`; changes take effect immediately.
7. Verify (next section), collect `GET /api/report` if a report is wanted.
8. `POST /api/stop` returns the network to normal and keeps clumsy alive for
   another round; `POST /api/quit` shuts it down.

curl (bash):

    curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/status
    curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/apply -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"lag":true,"lag-time":150}'
    curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/filter -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"filter":"udp and udp.DstPort == 7777"}'
    curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/quit

PowerShell (in Windows PowerShell 5.1 `curl` is an alias for
Invoke-WebRequest and takes different arguments; use these instead):

    Invoke-RestMethod http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/status
    Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/apply -ContentType application/json -Body '{"lag":true,"lag-time":150}'
    Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/filter -ContentType application/json -Body '{"filter":"udp and udp.DstPort == 7777"}'
    Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/quit

Starting it in the background from PowerShell:

    Start-Process clumsy.exe -ArgumentList '--timeout','600','--stats-console','0' -WindowStyle Hidden

REST conventions:

- Only GET and POST exist. POST bodies are JSON objects. Reads are GET,
  actions are POST; a wrong method or path returns a JSON error that says so.
- Every JSON reply has `"status"`: `"ok"` or `"error"` (with `"message"`).
- Booleans may be `true`/`false`, `"on"`/`"off"` or `1`/`0`.
- A token is only needed when clumsy was started with `--web-token` or a
  non-loopback `--web-bind`: send it as the `X-Clumsy-Token` header.
- `GET /api/stream` is a Server-Sent Events stream that never ends. From a
  script, poll `GET /api/stats` instead.


## Verifying that it is working

`GET /api/stats` while capturing:

    {"status":"ok","capturing":true,"elapsedMs":12040,"captured":5321,"sent":5108,
     "modules":{"lag":{"enabled":true,"affected":5321},"drop":{"enabled":true,"affected":213}, ...},
     "latency":{"count":5108,"p50":150,"p95":151,"p99":152, ...}, ...}

- `capturing` false: no capture is running. Start one with a filter.
- `captured` stays 0: the filter matches no traffic. Check the port, the
  protocol and the direction, and that the application is actually sending.
- `captured` grows but a module's `affected` stays 0: that module is off, its
  chance is 0, or its direction switches exclude the traffic.
- `latency` reports the delay lag and jitter really added.

The user-visible result (the application lagging, retrying, disconnecting)
is the real check; the counters only prove packets were touched.


## Scenarios: conditions that change over time

A scenario is a JSON array of steps. Each step has one trigger and any of the
keys `POST /api/apply` takes. It starts playing when the capture starts.

    [
      {"at": 0,  "lag": true, "lag-time": 80},
      {"at": 20, "drop": true, "drop-chance": 5},
      {"at": 40, "blackout": true, "blackout-duration": 3000, "blackout-gap": 20000},
      {"at": 70, "lag": false, "drop": false, "blackout": false},
      {"when": "captured_count", "op": ">=", "value": 20000, "bandwidth": true, "bandwidth-bandwidth": 200},
      {"at": 90, "repeat": 30, "times": 5, "drop-chance": 10}
    ]

- `at`: seconds since the capture started.
- `when` + `op` (`>=` `>` `<=` `<` `==`) + `value`: fire when a metric crosses a
  value. Metrics: `captured_count`, `sent_count`, `pps`, `elapsed_sec`,
  `lag_buf`, `jitter_buf`, `bandwidth_buf`, `affected:<module>`.
- `repeat`: fire again every N seconds; `times`: how many times (absent = forever).
- Keys starting with `_` are ignored, so `"_comment": "..."` is safe.
- Load it with `--scenario file.json`, or without a file:

      POST /api/scenario/loadinline
      {"scenario": [{"at":0,"lag":true,"lag-time":80},{"at":30,"lag":false}]}

  The reply lists `"warnings"` for unknown keys, bad values and unknown
  metrics - fix them before starting the capture.
- Steps are timed from the capture start and only run while capturing. Load
  the scenario first, then `POST /api/filter`; the scenario starts with it.


## Other outputs

- `--stats-log file.csv|file.json` with `--stats-interval <sec>`: time series.
- `--report-out report.html` (or `GET /api/report`): HTML session report.
- `--pcap-out file.pcap` (or `POST /api/pcap/start`): Wireshark-readable dump;
  `--pcap-stage pre|post|both` picks before or after the modules ran.
- `GET /metrics`: Prometheus text format.
- Profiles save a module setup under a name: `POST /api/profiles {"name":"x"}`,
  then `--profile x` or `POST /api/profiles/x/apply`. None ship by default.


## Platform notes

Windows
- Needs an Administrator console. `--elevate on` asks through a UAC prompt
  that a person has to accept; the elevated clumsy then opens in a new
  console window and the original process exits with 0, so its output is
  gone - follow it over REST.
- A second control channel exists on the named pipe `\\.\pipe\clumsy` (one
  JSON request, one JSON reply, e.g. `{"cmd":"get_status"}`, `{"cmd":"quit"}`).
  It does not use the network, so it still answers when a filter has cut
  off the REST port.

Linux
- Needs CAP_NET_ADMIN (run with sudo, or install the .deb which grants it).
- Add `--auto-iptables on`. Without it clumsy only sees traffic that an
  iptables NFQUEUE rule sends to it, and you would have to manage those
  rules yourself.
- The filter language is a subset: the keywords listed above, IPv4
  addresses only. Anything unsupported is rejected at start.
- The control channel is a Unix socket instead of a named pipe; its path is
  printed in the startup banner.
- Under WSL2 clumsy only sees traffic inside the WSL2 network namespace, not
  the Windows host's applications.


## If something goes wrong

| Symptom                                           | Cause and fix                                              |
|---------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| exit 2 immediately                                | Read stderr: it names the option. Check `clumsy --help`.    |
| exit 3, "needs Administrator rights"              | Not elevated. Ask the user to run the terminal as Administrator. |
| exit 3, filter error                              | The filter did not parse. Simplify it and retry.           |
| exit 4, "already an instance"                     | Use the running one (`GET /api/status`) or `POST /api/quit` it. |
| REST connection refused                           | Not started yet (poll /api/health), a different `--web-port`, or `--web off`. |
| REST was working, now times out                   | Your filter is shaping the control port. Wait for `--timeout`, or send `{"cmd":"quit"}` to the named pipe. Exclude the port next time. |
| 401 from every endpoint                           | A token is set. Send the `X-Clumsy-Token` header.          |
| "status":"ok" but nothing changes                 | No capture is running, or check `unknownKeys` / `warnings` in the reply. |
| The whole machine has no network                  | Filter too broad with heavy loss or blackout. `POST /api/quit`, or wait for `--timeout`. |
